questions.question: If a bus has a restroom, it must have:

options.text: An emergency buzzer.
A window.
Two exits.
Paper towels.

questions.correctAnswerText: An emergency buzzer.
questions.explanation: Bus restrooms must have an emergency buzzer.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror lets the driver see:

options.text: What is happening inside the bus.
What is happening outside the bus.
Traffic conditions.
The door opening and closing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is happening inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror helps the driver watch passengers on the bus.

questions.question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers:

options.text: Do not need to stop.
Do not need to stop, but must slow down to 25 mph below the speed limit.
Do not need to stop, but must open the door to listen for trains.
Must stop and look for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and look for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, stop 15 to 50 feet from the track. Look and listen for trains. Only go forward when you are sure no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, if police are directing traffic, if a green light shows, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: Buses must never carry ____ where passengers sit.

options.text: Small arms ammunition
An oxygen tank
Radioactive materials
Passengers who are drunk

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials in the passenger area.

questions.question: Which of these causes the most student deaths per year?

options.text: Students getting on or off a school bus
Accidents with drunk drivers
Accidents from careless driving
Accidents from drivers ignoring traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students getting on or off a school bus
questions.explanation: More students die each year boarding or leaving school buses than while riding inside them.

questions.question: When passengers ride a bus, the aisle should:

options.text: Allow items to be left there.
Allow items if everyone is seated.
Be clear of all obstacles.
Allow items if they have an orange cone next to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be clear of all obstacles.
questions.explanation: Do not allow passengers to leave items in the aisle while the bus is moving. Aisles and stairs must always be clear.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that was left alone, you should:

options.text: Wash the outside.
Remove air from the tires.
Check the inside for damage.
Look for animals that may have boarded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the inside for damage.
questions.explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses. Walk through the bus to check the inside for any damage.

questions.question: The area to the left of a school bus is dangerous because:

options.text: The sun reflects off the left side.
Passing vehicles are on the left.
It is hard to see the left side.
There is no door on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing vehicles are on the left.
questions.explanation: The left side of a school bus is especially dangerous because passing vehicles travel there.

questions.question: Before driving a bus, you must:

options.text: Read the last inspection report.
Wash the outside.
Clean the inside.
Count the seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the last inspection report.
questions.explanation: Always read the inspection report from the previous driver before driving a bus. Only drive if any reported problems have been fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: To make sure a bus is safe before driving, you should:

options.text: Read the inspection report from the last driver.
Kick the tires.
Ask your supervisor if it is safe.
Ask passengers if they feel safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the inspection report from the last driver.
questions.explanation: Always read the inspection report from the previous driver before driving a bus. Only drive if any reported problems have been fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing while driving a school bus, what should you do?

options.text: Assume you will hear a train coming.
Only rely on signals to know if a train is coming.
Open the door and listen for a train.
Go ahead right away after a train passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door and listen for a train.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on signals at railroad crossings. Tell passengers to be quiet, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. Before crossing the tracks, check for trains coming from both directions.

questions.question: What must buses never carry?

options.text: Small arms ammunition.
Soft drinks.
Medical supplies.
Tear gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tear gas.
questions.explanation: Tear gas and irritating materials can never be carried on a bus. Some hazardous materials may be allowed under certain conditions. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D and emergency medical supplies are permitted.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?

options.text: One
Three
Six
Nine

questions.correctAnswerText: Nine
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are divided into nine classes. Each class describes what type of danger the material presents.

questions.question: If a bus has a brake and accelerator interlock system, how should it be used?

options.text: Turn it off in most situations.
Use it only in bad weather.
Never use it instead of the parking brake.
Use it to operate the rear door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never use it instead of the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Some buses have a brake and accelerator interlock system that applies the brakes and idles the throttle when the rear door opens. This system should not replace the parking brake.

questions.question: When driving a charter bus, what should a driver do?

options.text: Explain how to use the TVs if the bus has them.
Not let passengers board until the scheduled departure time.
Let passengers board early to get ahead of schedule.
Tell passengers to sit in the back first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not let passengers board until the scheduled departure time.
questions.explanation: Do not let passengers board before the scheduled departure time. This helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.

questions.question: What is true about loading a school bus?

options.text: It is not dangerous.
It does not need supervision.
It should be done as fast as possible.
It can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading or unloading of school buses than while riding on them. School bus drivers must follow safety procedures during loading and unloading.

questions.question: How far away should a bus stop from students at a bus stop?

options.text: About 100 feet
At least 50 feet
At least 10 feet
Less than 10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Stop at least 10 feet away from students at a bus stop. This makes students walk toward the bus so you can watch them safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss a student's stop when dropping them off after school?

options.text: Back up to the stop.
Follow the procedures your school has set.
Do not worry about the student.
Stop quickly and let them out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the procedures your school has set.
questions.explanation: Do not back up to a missed stop. Instead, follow your school's established procedures.

questions.question: When should rules about passenger comfort, like smoking rules, be shared?

options.text: Only if someone breaks a rule.
Only if a passenger asks about something.
At the beginning of the trip.
One-on-one with each passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the beginning of the trip.
questions.explanation: Many buses have rules about smoking, drinking, and music players. Explaining these rules at the start of a trip helps prevent problems later.

questions.question: What should the stairwell of a bus be used for?

options.text: It can store items if needed.
It can be used as a seat if needed.
It should store small items.
It must stay clear at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must stay clear at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep the aisles and stairwell of a bus clear at all times. Do not let passengers store bags in these areas.
